title: Load balancing
summary: Load balancing distributes requests across service instances according to a routing policy.
overview: A balancer chooses eligible backends using health and load signals. Equal request counts do not imply equal work when request costs differ.
why: Uneven routing can overload one instance while others have spare capacity.
example: An API pool drains an instance before shutdown and routes new requests to healthy instances with available capacity.
judgment: Choose a policy that fits request cost, connection behavior, and health-check limitations.
next: Do long-lived connections prevent our traffic from spreading across newly added instances?
